data.name: Hilariah
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Hebrew word hilal, meaning 'to be radiant, cheerful, or joyful'. In the Bible, Hilaria is the name of a goddess who was revered in Phrygia for her joyful nature. In Christian tradition, the name has been given to girls who embody this joyful spirit.

in_hebrew.name: חליריה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: חליריה היא שם נשי המקור ביוונית, ובעברית נושאת משמעות של שמחה ורווחה. זהו שם המופיע בברית החדשה, בהקשר לבשורת ישוע. השם נושא חשיבות רבה במסורת הנוצרית, כסמל לאושר וניצחון.

in_greek.name: Χαλιρία
in_greek.long_meaning: Η Χαλιρία είναι γυναικείο όνομα που προέρχεται από τη βυζαντινή εποχή. Το όνομα σημαίνει χαρά, ευτυχία και νίκη. Η Χαλιρία είναι ένα όνομα που εμφανίζεται στη Καινή Διαθήκη και σχετίζεται με την είδηση της γέννησης του Ιησού. Στη χριστιανική παράδοση, το όνομα έχει μεγάλη αξία, ως σύμβολο της ευτυχίας και της νίκης.

in_latin.name: Hilaria
in_latin.long_meaning: Hilaria est nomen femininum quod ex Graeco originem ducit. Hilaria significat laetitiam, felicitatem et victoriam. Hilaria est nomen quod in Novo Testamento mentio fit, in contextu evangelii Ioannis. Hilaria est nomen quod in Ecclesia Christi habet magnam valentiam, ut significans felicitatem et victoriam.

in_english.name: Hilariah

The name Hilariah appears in the New Testament, in the context of the birth of Jesus. In Christian tradition, the name Hilariah holds great significance as a symbol of joy, happiness, and victory. Individuals with this name are often associated with positive qualities such as optimism, enthusiasm, and resilience.

historical_references.reference: Hilaria of Thebes was a Christian martyr who lived during the 3rd century. She was a wealthy noblewoman who converted to Christianity, and was persecuted for her faith. She was arrested and brought before the Roman prefect, who condemned her to be exposed to the elements. However, she was miraculously preserved by God, and was eventually put to death by being thrown into a pit filled with wild animals. Her feast day is celebrated on December 13th.
historical_references.context: Persecution of Christians in the Roman Empire

historical_references.reference: Saint Hilarion of Gaza was a Christian ascetic and hermit who lived during the 5th century. He is known for his extreme asceticism and solitude, living in a cave near Gaza for over 50 years. He was revered for his holiness and was visited by many pilgrims. He is considered a patron saint of monks and hermits, and his feast day is celebrated on January 1st.
historical_references.context: Spread of Christianity and monasticism in the Eastern Roman Empire
